summary:
MARS-TO-EARTH ANALOG DATABASE

Project Name
An interactive app that matches Martian environments with similar Earth ecosystems, such as hyper-arid deserts, polar permafrost and acidic rivers.

OUR CHALLENGE & SOLUTION
Challenge: Understand how organisms and environments survive radiation, water scarcity and freezing temperatures on Mars.

Solution: The app compares Mars with familiar terrestrial ecosystems and makes complex space data easier to understand.

KEY FEATURES

* Side-by-side comparison of Martian landscapes and Earth analogs.
* Atmospheric insights including oxygen concentration, CO₂ levels and atmospheric pressure.
* Gravity simulator showing Mars at about 38% of Earth’s gravity.
* Rover exploration and scientific criteria for selecting analog environments.

WHY IT MATTERS
The project can support NASA astronauts and researchers by helping them train, test equipment and prepare for deep-space missions. It connects planetary science with practical Earth-based testing and future habitation planning.

DATA, DEVELOPMENT & LINKS
Development: UI improvements, Compare section, Rover Exploration, scientific criteria, Android integration and data integration.

Data: NASA HiRISE, CRISM and THEMIS datasets, combined with terrestrial coordinates and analog data.

details: Mars-to-Earth Analog Database: This innovative web and mobile application offers a completely gesture-controlled (touchless) interactive map for safe and hygienic hands-free navigation across planetary surfaces. Using official data from NASA (including NASA POWER and Mars Trek), the system analyzes soil, climate, and terrain, allowing users to compare Earth analog sites with Martian regions through the Replicate & Compare and Space Log features. The project aims to facilitate scientific research, improve access to space data, and support future mission planning in a completely intuitive way.
